title: Michael Levin frog embryo in a Faraday cage
summary: Jesse Michels tells of Michael Levin frog embryo in a Faraday cage, about recent at Tufts, and frames it as the host. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: you put a frog embryo for example in a Faraday cage so you eliminate you know all electromagnetic interference it won't grow correctly

plain: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, describes work linked to Michael Levin, a biologist at Tufts University. Michels says that if you put a frog embryo inside a Faraday cage, a metal enclosure that blocks outside electric and magnetic fields, it won't grow correctly. He brings it up to suggest that living things may depend on electromagnetic signals in ways science is only starting to understand.
